title: Market Pulse
body_html:
This post reflects my current views on the market, sectors, and internal breadth/momentum. Expect candid, data-driven analysis, peppered with personal insights drawn from years of trading experience. I aim to provide value in every edition, helping you to see the market through a clearer, more informed lens.

What You Can Expect

  • In-Depth Market Analysis: A thorough examination of market trends, key indices, and pivotal turning points.

  • Sector Spotlights: A closer look at the hottest (and not-so-hot) sectors, highlighting opportunities and risks.

  • Breadth and Momentum Insights: Understanding the underlying strength of the market through breadth indicators and momentum metrics.

  • Themes and Setups: A look at the top stocks in terms of relative strength, momentum, trend, volatility, and liquidity to spot themes, setups, and opportunities

Exclusive Features

  • Interactive Spreadsheet: Alongside each post, I’ll link a detailed spreadsheet that tracks breadth and momentum metrics. This will allow you to follow along with the data and see the trends I’m analyzing day-by-day.

  • Quick Video Commentary: To complement the metrics, I’ll also be posting a quick video commentary several days a week. This will provide a more dynamic overview of the market, offering you additional context and clarity.

Market Metrics

Market Backdrop: Negative

The market is still in a defensive, downward trend. All four major indices are trading below their 10-, 20-, and 50-day moving averages, and the overall price action remains bearish. For the outlook to improve, the indices need to move back above these key levels and start forming a stronger structure. This would mean first ending the pattern of lower lows, then forming higher lows and higher highs. Until that happens, it makes sense to stay cautious rather than take on aggressive long positions.

Sector performance is also lackluster. Energy remains the strongest sector, supported by ongoing tensions in the Middle East, which are keeping oil prices high. This strength in Energy may continue for now. Most other sectors are still in downtrends, with their 10- and 20-day moving averages sloping down and a pattern of lower highs and lower lows. There are few leaders, which makes a broad and lasting market rally less likely and means investors need to be selective.

Market breadth and momentum continue to show weakness. There are still many new lows and very few new highs, which points to ongoing selling and weak demand. For the market to stabilize, improvement needs to spread and last. We should see more new highs over several days, stronger upward moves, and fewer new lows. If these changes happen, it would be an early sign that the market is moving from decline toward stabilization and recovery.

1) Trend & Market Structure

The market is still in a confirmed downtrend. With all four major indices below their 10/20/50-day moving averages and price action remaining bearish, long-side expectancy is low.

Tactical guidance

  • Operate in defense-first mode: keep long exposure 0–20% of normal risk (or 0% if you don’t have true RS outliers).

  • Do not assume a bottom. The market must prove stabilization by:

    • stopping lower lows, then

    • forming higher lows, then

    • reclaiming the 20-day, and ultimately the 50-day.

  • Treat rallies into declining 10/20-day moving averages as resistance and potential trim zones—not automatic buy signals.

Risk trigger

  • If indices continue making lower lows or lose recent support levels with volume, remain cash-heavy and avoid “hope trades.”

2) Breadth & Momentum (Primary Throttle)

Breadth remains weak: many new lows and few new highs. That’s a classic environment where breakouts fail and bounces are unreliable.

Tactical guidance

  • Keep trade frequency low and standards high.

  • Re-engagement criteria (what you need to see):

    • new highs expanding for several sessions

    • new lows contracting meaningfully

    • upside expansion beginning to dominate downside expansion

  • Until then, treat any strength as tactical and assume follow-through remains inconsistent.

3) Sector Focus: Narrow Leadership, High Selectivity

Energy is the only clear leader, likely supported by geopolitical tensions and oil price strength. Most other sectors remain in downtrends with declining short-term MAs and poor structure.

Tactical guidance

  • If you participate, focus primarily on:

    • Energy leaders with clean bases and defined risk

    • isolated RS outliers in other sectors that are holding structure better than the market

  • Do not chase broad sector exposure in weak conditions.

  • Be extremely cautious in weak “risk-on” groups (Tech/Consumer/Financials) until they stop deteriorating and rebuild structure.

4) Stock Selection & Entries (If You Trade at All)

In a downtrend, your edge is structure + relative strength + tight risk.

Prioritize

  • Stocks holding above their 10/20-day and resisting the decline

  • Tight consolidations/bases (not V-bounces)

  • Support-based entries with clear invalidation (pattern low / 20-day)

Avoid

  • Breakouts (low hit rate in weak breadth)

  • V-shaped rebounds without basing

  • Anything below declining 20/50-day moving averages

5) Trade Management & Risk Controls

In this tape, management needs to be tight and fast.

  • Position size: ¼ to ½ normal maximum

  • Stops: hard, structural stops below support/pattern lows

  • Take partial profits quickly; don’t expect long trends

  • If a trade doesn’t work quickly, exit—no “giving it room” in a bearish market

6) Exposure Controls & Re-Engagement Plan

Base case (now): defensive

  • Exposure: 0–20%

  • Cash: 80–100%

  • Trades: rare, tactical only

Early stabilization

  • Lower lows stop + new lows contract + new highs begin expanding
    → test exposure 20–35% in the strongest RS names only

Confirmed repair

  • Indices reclaim 20-day then 50-day + breadth thrust + leadership broadens beyond Energy
    → scale toward 35–60% gradually

Bottom Line

This remains a defensive environment. With indices below key moving averages, breadth weak, and leadership narrow, the priority is capital protection and patience. Stay mostly in cash, only trade the best relative strength outliers with tight risk, and wait for the market to prove stabilization through improved breadth and reclaimed moving averages before increasing exposure.
